latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Fibrin-platelet-microbial thrombus on endocardial surface (native or prosthetic), central pathologic lesion of IE; biofilm protects organisms from antibiotics and host defenses, sustaining bacteremia and embolic risk

Continuous shedding of organisms from vegetation into bloodstream; defining feature of IE distinguishing it from transient bacteremia; persistence beyond 48-72h on appropriate therapy implies inadequate source control or resistant pathogen
Direct microbial and inflammatory destruction of valve leaflets, chordae, and annular tissue producing perforation, flail, regurgitation; drives acute heart failure and surgical indications

Detachment of vegetation fragments embolizing to systemic (left-sided IE: brain, spleen, kidney, coronary, mesentery, limb) or pulmonary (right-sided IE) circulation; produces ischemic infarcts and metastatic infection
Spread of infection beyond valve annulus into myocardium producing abscess, pseudoaneurysm, fistula, or conduction tissue invasion (esp. aortic root); strong indication for surgery

Chronic antigenemia drives circulating immune complex formation depositing in glomeruli (GN with hematuria/proteinuria, low complement), skin (Osler nodes, Janeway lesions partly embolic), retina (Roth spots)

Sudden severe aortic or mitral regurgitation from valve destruction without time for chamber compensation produces acute pulmonary edema, cardiogenic shock; leading cause of in-hospital mortality and #1 indication for early surgery
Septic embolic seeding of arterial vasa vasorum producing weakened arterial wall and aneurysm, especially intracranial (MCA bifurcations), with rupture risk producing catastrophic hemorrhage
Total viable microbial load within vegetation and bloodstream; drives all downstream inflammatory, embolic, and destructive processes
Hepatocyte-driven acute phase response producing CRP, fibrinogen, ferritin elevation and anemia of inflammation through hepcidin
Bacterial PAMP/DAMP-driven granulopoiesis with left shift, neutrophilia, procalcitonin release
Probability that organism is MRSA, VRE, ceftriaxone-resistant viridans, or other resistant strain reducing efficacy of standard empiric therapy

Hematogenous seeding to distant sites (spondylodiscitis, septic arthritis, psoas/splenic abscess, septic pulmonary emboli in right-sided IE) producing secondary deep foci that may require independent source control

supportive_care: Obtain three sets of blood cultures from separate venipunctures over 30-60 minutes (>1-2 hours apart for subacute presentations) before antibiotics whenever clinically safe
Echocardiography: TTE first, TEE if TTE non-diagnostic, prosthetic valve, intracardiac device, or high suspicion; repeat TEE for new complications or persistent bacteremia
Apply Modified Duke Criteria (or 2023 Duke-ISCVID) integrating microbiology, imaging, and clinical findings
Daily blood cultures until bacteremia clears, then weekly to confirm sustained sterilization
Cardiology and cardiothoracic surgery consultation for all confirmed IE; consider Endocarditis Team (heart valve team)
Infectious diseases consultation for antibiotic selection, duration, and source-control planning
Continuous cardiac monitoring for new conduction block (suggesting perivalvular extension)
Daily exam for new murmur, embolic phenomena, neurologic change, peripheral stigmata
Brain imaging (MRI preferred) when neurologic signs or for surgical planning in left-sided IE
Whole-body imaging (CT, FDG-PET/CT) to identify metastatic foci and silent emboli
Therapeutic drug monitoring: vancomycin AUC, aminoglycoside peak/trough
Renal function and electrolyte monitoring; dose-adjust nephrotoxic agents
Liver function monitoring with rifampin, nafcillin, ceftriaxone
Dental evaluation and extraction of carious teeth in viridans streptococcal IE before completing treatment
Colonoscopy after S. gallolyticus IE to evaluate for colorectal neoplasia
Address modifiable risks: catheter removal/replacement, IV drug use counseling and harm-reduction/treatment referral, dental restoration

DVT prophylaxis weighed against bleeding/embolic stroke risk; avoid full-dose anticoagulation in S. aureus left-sided IE due to hemorrhagic transformation risk; for patients on chronic anticoagulation with mechanical valves, individualize after multidisciplinary review
Heart failure management for valve-related decompensation: diuresis, afterload reduction; preserve euvolemia pre-surgery
Nutritional support; address weight loss and hypoalbuminemia
Counseling on long IV antibiotic course (typically 4-6 weeks), home OPAT considerations after stabilization
Education on lifelong endocarditis prophylaxis for highest-risk patients (prior IE, prosthetic valve, certain congenital lesions) before high-risk dental procedures
Vaccination review (pneumococcal, influenza)
Plan post-discharge surveillance echocardiogram and clinical follow-up to detect recurrence or late valvular complications
